description: ODC (E/D coverage): the LIFECYCLE of a timer that ALREADY EXISTED. Nothing is created here: the base is job:timer-action, and everything this job does is TOUCH the WfCovOverdueSweep that came from there -- change the schedule through both routes, change the TimeoutInMinutes, the priority and the description, rename it and delete it. The question the job answers: the census (anvil-odc census --oml .local/lane-odc/jobs/timer-action.oml) marks ITimer.ScheduleConfiguration (ISchedule) and ISchedule.ScheduleItems as readOnly, and inside each item MinuteValues/HourValues are also readOnly -- only Interval and WhenPublished are writable, and neither is the schedule. So THROUGH WHERE is the schedule changed? Through the PARENT: the ITimer has two write properties, CronSchedule and Schedule, and each of them makes the platform THROW AWAY the ISchedule tree and build another (the IMinute/IHour come back with NEW KEYS, and that is the proof that nobody edits the readOnly child: it is output, never input). The two routes are inverses of each other and each one rewrites the other property. It closes with rename (the derived child WakeTimerAction follows the name by itself) and delete (the timer leaves with no consumers; the server action it woke is left orphaned, and the Verify says so -- and that is why there is a declared message).

expectedMessages.why: Deleting the timer is deleting the ONLY consumer of WfCovTask_SweepOverdue: the logic it woke stays in the module with nobody calling it. The warning is the declared consequence of the delete, not a defect of the job -- the last usages proves it with real=0. Deleting it as well would also silence the warning, but this job is the lifecycle of the TIMER and the evidence that deleting a timer does not take the logic with it is worth more than the silence.

ops._why: 1. INHERITED, not created: the module arrives at this job already with ONE timer, the one from job:timer-action. Compare with the find at the end.
the state that came from the base: CronSchedule '15 3 * * *', the derived Schedule '03:15', TimeoutInMinutes 20, Priority Normal
the readOnly child of the census: ScheduleItems has 5 items and the only property it lets be written is WhenPublished
KEEP THIS KEY: Interval AtOrOn and MinuteValues 1 (minute 15). Another one will come back after the first set.
the '*' of the cron is not an absence: it is an IDayOfWeek with Interval Any and zero values

2. ROUTE A: write the cron on the PARENT. This is the path the census hides -- the ISchedule tree is readOnly because the one who builds it is the platform, from this string (FromCronExpression). In 5 fields: every 15 minutes, from 8 to 18, Monday to Friday.
both sides moved together: CronSchedule is the text we wrote and Schedule, which is DERIVED, expanded into the readable list ('08:00 08:15 ... Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri') instead of the previous '03:15'

THE PROOF: the key of the IMinute is NOT the one above. The object was not edited -- it was thrown away and another was built, now with Interval 'Every' (the */15) instead of 'AtOrOn'. A set on the readOnly child could not have done this.
the same for the hour: Interval 'Between' and HourValues 2 (the start and the end of the 8-18), also with a new key
the whole tree rebuilt: five items, because FromCronExpression also creates the Any placeholders (IMonth, IDayOfMonth)

3. ROUTE B, the inverse: Schedule is also writable, and it is not just pretty text -- writing the readable time makes the platform generate the cron. It serves the common case ('runs at 07:45') without spelling out cron.
and CronSchedule appeared by itself as '45 7 * * *': the two properties are two faces of the SAME tree, each write regenerates the other face

DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO ROUTES: through here the tree ends up with TWO items (IMinute, IHour) and not five -- the builder from the readable time does not create Any placeholders. Same schedule, different shape inside; do not count items to infer the schedule.
4. the rest of the edit, on values that already existed: 20 -> 45
Normal -> High

ops.value: Cobertura E: varre tarefas vencidas de 15 em 15 minutos no horario de trabalho

ops._why: the four edits in a single read-back; note that the Description still talks about the */15 that is no longer there: text written by hand never follows the model
so the fix is by hand, on the other side: restore the schedule that the Description describes
final state of the edit, consistent with the description
5. BEFORE RENAMING: a timer is a leaf of the graph -- nobody consumes it (real 0). It is the one that consumes.
on the other side: the action has exactly ONE real consumer, this timer

ops.name: WfCovOverdueNightly
ops._why: 6. REFACTOR: consumers 0 and expressionsRewritten 0 do not mean nothing moved -- they mean nothing POINTS to a timer. What moves is what is INSIDE it.

the derived child followed by itself: the IActionSignature of the timer went from WakeWfCovOverdueSweep to WakeWfCovOverdueNightly. There is no op asking for this; it is the platform maintaining what is its own.
and the link to the action survived the rename, now with the new name in the path: consumers are held by KEY, not by name
7. DELETE: without force and with brokenConsumers 0, because the usages above had already said nobody consumes it. Deleting what has consumers is the other half, proven in delete-logic-consumers.
the proof of the delete, closing the arc of the first op: where there was a timer the module now returns an empty list

8. WHAT THE DELETE COST: the action the timer woke is still in the module, but went from real 1 to real 0. Deleting the scheduler does not delete the scheduled logic -- and the UnusedUserAction declared in expectedMessages is the Verify saying the same.
